candidates: When adding a JSDoc comment to a typed property, ensure it provides information beyond what the type signature already encodes. Comments that merely restate what a union variant or optional marker already expresses (e.g., explaining that an `unknown` variant exists when that variant is already visible in the type) add noise without value and should be removed or replaced with genuinely additive documentation.

Every variant in a string-literal union type (such as the `KnownAgentName` union in `code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts`) must be reachable from at least one runtime code path in the same module. If a new agent name is added to the union, the corresponding detection logic in `detectExplicitAgent` (or equivalent) must be implemented in the same PR; otherwise remove the variant until detection is ready.

Test `it()` description strings must accurately reflect the actual return value and type being asserted. If the function under test returns `undefined`, say so in the description (e.g., 'returns undefined when there are no signals') rather than using terminology from an unrelated type shape (e.g., 'returns isAgent=false'). Mismatched descriptions make failures harder to diagnose.
